text: The repository tracks automated tests next to the code they cover.
why: Untested code has no executable statement of what it must do, so every change is a guess.

enforcement.run: git ls-files | grep -qE '(^|/)(tests?|__tests__|spec)/|(_test\.go|_test\.py|(^|/)test_[^/]*\.py|\.(test|spec)\.[cm]?[jt]sx?)$'

text: The repository declares one test command that runs its tests, never a placeholder.
why: Agents and CI run what the repository declares; a missing or placeholder test command makes every run a silent no-op.

enforcement.run: if [ -s package.json ]; then node -e 'const t=(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync("package.json","utf8")).scripts||{}).test||"";process.exit(t.trim()===""||/no test specified/.test(t)?1:0)'; elif [ -f composer.json ] || [ -f phpunit.xml ] || [ -f phpunit.xml.dist ]; then if [ -f phpunit.xml ] || [ -f phpunit.xml.dist ]; then true; else node -e 'const s=(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync("composer.json","utf8")).scripts||{}).test;process.exit(s===undefined||/no test specified/.test(JSON.stringify(s))?1:0)'; fi; elif [ -f go.mod ]; then git ls-files | grep -q '_test\.go$'; elif [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then true; elif [ -f pyproject.toml ] || [ -f setup.cfg ] || [ -f setup.py ] || [ -f tox.ini ] || [ -f pytest.ini ]; then git ls-files | grep -qE '(^|/)(test_[^/]*|[^/]*_test)\.py$'; else grep -qE '^test:' Makefile 2>/dev/null; fi

text: The test command exits non-zero when a test fails: no `|| true`, `; exit 0` or leading `-` masks its status.
why: A test run whose failure exits 0 turns every red tree into a delivered one.

enforcement.run: { [ ! -s package.json ] || node -e 'const s=JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync("package.json","utf8")).scripts||{};const bad=Object.entries(s).filter(([k,v])=>/^test/.test(k)&&/\|\|\s*(true|:|exit 0)|;\s*exit 0\s*$/.test(String(v)));if(bad.length){console.error("masked: "+bad.map(b=>b[0]).join(", "));process.exit(1)}'; } && { [ ! -f Makefile ] || awk '/^test[a-zA-Z0-9_-]*:/{t=1;next} /^[^\t]/{t=0} t&&(/\|\| *(true|:)/||/^\t-/){bad=1} END{exit bad}' Makefile; }

text: Continuous integration runs the tests on every pull request.
why: Only a check on the proposed head proves the merged tree; local green on another tree proves nothing.

enforcement.run: ci=$(cat .github/workflows/*.yml .github/workflows/*.yaml .gitlab-ci.yml 2>/dev/null); printf '%s\n' "$ci" | grep -qE 'pull_request|merge_request' && printf '%s\n' "$ci" | grep -qE '(pytest|tox|nox|unittest|(npm|pnpm|yarn|bun)( run)? test|vitest|jest|node --test|go test|cargo test|make test|uv run|hatch run|poetry run|phpunit|composer( run)? test)|uses: *[^ ]*/[^ ]*ci\.ya?ml'

text: No tracked file is a credential file or holds a private key or provider token.
why: A secret in git history leaks to every clone and stays there after the file is deleted.

enforcement.run: ! git ls-files | grep -vE '\.env\.(example|sample|template|dist)$' | grep -qE '(^|/)(\.env(\.[^/]*)?|id_rsa|id_ecdsa|id_ed25519|[^/]*\.pem|[^/]*\.p12|\.netrc|\.git-credentials)$' && ! git grep -qIE -e '-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----' -e 'AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}' -e 'gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}' -e 'xox[abp]-[0-9A-Za-z-]{20,}'

text: Installed dependencies, caches and bytecode are never tracked.
why: Tracked install output bloats every clone and drifts from the lockfile it should come from.

enforcement.run: ! git ls-files | grep -qE '(^|/)(node_modules|__pycache__|\.venv|venv|\.pytest_cache|\.mypy_cache|\.ruff_cache|\.tox)/|\.py[co]$'

text: The ignore rules cover the dependency and build directories of the stack.
why: An unignored install directory is one `git add .` away from being committed.

enforcement.run: if [ -s package.json ]; then git check-ignore -q --no-index node_modules/probe; else git check-ignore -q --no-index __pycache__/probe.pyc && { git check-ignore -q --no-index .venv/probe || git check-ignore -q --no-index venv/probe; }; fi

text: A formatter or linter is configured for the stack, so style is checked by a tool, not by review.
why: Style left to review costs a round trip per nit and is applied unevenly.

enforcement.run: for f in biome.json biome.jsonc .eslintrc .eslintrc.* eslint.config.* .prettierrc .prettierrc.* prettier.config.* ruff.toml .ruff.toml .flake8 .pylintrc .golangci.yml .golangci.yaml .golangci.toml rustfmt.toml .rustfmt.toml phpcs.xml phpcs.xml.dist .phpcs.xml phpstan.neon phpstan.neon.dist .php-cs-fixer.php .php-cs-fixer.dist.php pint.json psalm.xml; do [ -e "$f" ] && exit 0; done; grep -qE '^\[tool\.(ruff|black|flake8|pylint)' pyproject.toml 2>/dev/null || grep -qE '"(@biomejs/biome|eslint|prettier)"' package.json 2>/dev/null || cat .github/workflows/*.y*ml 2>/dev/null | grep -qE 'gofmt|go vet|golangci|cargo fmt|cargo clippy'

text: The README states how to run the tests.
why: A newcomer or agent that cannot find the test command ships untested changes.

enforcement.run: cat README* readme* 2>/dev/null | grep -qiE '(pytest|tox|nox|unittest|(npm|pnpm|yarn|bun)( run)? test|vitest|jest|node --test|go test|cargo test|make test|uv run|hatch run|poetry run|phpunit|composer( run)? test)'

text: No tracked file holds an unresolved merge conflict marker.
why: A committed conflict marker breaks the build or, in prose and data, silently ships both sides.

text: A repository keeps one instruction file for agents, AGENTS.md; any other agent instruction file is a link to it or points to it.
why: Two instruction files drift apart and agents follow whichever they read first.

enforcement.run: for f in CLAUDE.md GEMINI.md .cursorrules .github/copilot-instructions.md; do [ ! -e "$f" ] || [ "$(readlink "$f")" = AGENTS.md ] || grep -q 'AGENTS.md' "$f" || { echo "$f does not point to AGENTS.md" >&2; exit 1; }; done

text: The test suite gives the same verdict on a clean checkout: no test depends on untracked local state such as an earlier build or the enclosing repository.
why: A suite that reads a local build or the surrounding repository is green on one machine and red in CI or in a fresh worktree, so its verdict proves nothing about the change.

enforcement.run: [ ! -s package.json ] || node -e 'const fs=require("fs"),cp=require("child_process");const s=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("package.json","utf8")).scripts||{};if(/\b(build|tsc|tsup|esbuild|rollup|webpack)\b/.test([s.pretest,s.test].join(" ")))process.exit(0);const files=cp.execFileSync("git",["ls-files","-z"],{encoding:"utf8"}).split("\0");if(files.some(f=>/(^|\/)dist\//.test(f)))process.exit(0);const bad=files.filter(f=>/\.(test|spec)\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$|(^|\/)(tests?|__tests__)\/.*\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/.test(f)&&fs.existsSync(f)&&/["\x27`][^"\x27`\s]*\bdist\/[^"\x27`\s]*\.[cm]?js["\x27`]/.test(fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8")));if(bad.length){console.error("tests read untracked dist/ output but the test script builds nothing: "+bad.slice(0,3).join(", "));process.exit(1)}'

text: A fixed defect gets its regression test at the lowest layer that reproduces it.
why: Low-layer tests fail fast and name the broken unit.

text: When a task names an input or output format, at least one test feeds the plainest hand-written example of that format exactly as the task words it.
why: A reader tested only on its own tool's output rejects the short, plain forms real callers send.

text: Every integration or forward is tested against its real receiver or a verbatim capture of the receiver's output, never against a hand-made imitation.
why: An integration is only proven where it is received.

text: Files, functions, tests and work are named by purpose and role, never by phase, ticket, round, date or version.
why: Phase and ticket names lose their meaning as soon as the phase or ticket ends.

enforcement.run: ! git ls-files | grep -vE '(^|/)fixtures/' | grep -E '\.(ts|tsx|js|mjs|cjs|py|php|sh|go)$' | grep -qiE '(^|[-_./])((phase|slice|round|ticket|sprint)[-_.]?[0-9]+|t-[a-z0-9]{7})([-_.]|$)|20[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}|[-_.]v[0-9]+[-_.]'

text: Every error path has a stated exit code (64 usage, 65 invalid data, 70 internal, 75 temporary) and a message on stderr.
why: Callers and agents branch on exit codes; an unstated one makes a failure look like success or the wrong failure.

enforcement.run: ! git grep -qIE '(catch[^{]*\{[^}]*process\.exit\([[:space:]]*0|except[^:]*:[[:space:]]*(sys\.)?exit\([[:space:]]*0)' -- '*.ts' '*.tsx' '*.js' '*.jsx' '*.mjs' '*.cjs' '*.py'

text: Values that may hold credentials, multiline ones included, are redacted before they are logged, persisted or forwarded.
why: A secret written to a log or a record leaks to everyone who can read it later.

enforcement.run: ! git grep -qIiE '(console\.(log|error|warn|info|debug)|logger\.[a-z]+|logging\.[a-z]+|print|echo)[[:space:]]*\(?.*(password|passwd|secret|api_?key|private_?key|auth_?token|access_?token)[A-Za-z_]*[[:space:]]*[,)+}]' -- '*.ts' '*.tsx' '*.js' '*.jsx' '*.mjs' '*.cjs' '*.py' '*.php' '*.sh' ':(exclude)test' ':(exclude)tests' ':(exclude)__tests__' ':(exclude)*.test.*' ':(exclude)*.spec.*' ':(exclude)*/fixtures/*'

text: Never change the git stash stack with a bare `git stash` or `git stash pop`; set work aside with a commit.
why: Every worktree of a repository shares one stash stack, so a bare pop can take another lane's edits.

enforcement.run: ! git grep -qIE 'git[[:space:]]+stash([[:space:]]+(push|save|pop|apply|drop|clear)([^A-Za-z]|$)|[[:space:]]*($|[;&|)"]))' -- '*.sh' '*.bash' '*.yml' '*.yaml' Makefile justfile package.json

text: Commit subjects since the repository adopted krn are semantic: `type(scope): outcome` with a conventional type such as feat, fix, docs, chore or refactor.
why: A typed subject lets history, changelogs and review tooling classify a change without reading its diff.

enforcement.run: ! git rev-parse -q --verify HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! { a=$(git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- krn.json 2>/dev/null | tail -1); git log --no-merges -n 20 --format=%s ${a:+$a..HEAD}; } | grep -vE '^(Revert "|(feat|fix|docs|chore|refactor|test|perf|build|ci|style|revert)(\([^)]+\))?!?: )' | grep -q .

text: Tracked shell scripts run ssh and scp with `-o BatchMode=yes` and apt-get install with `-y`, so they fail instead of waiting for a prompt.
why: An agent or CI job has no one to answer a password, host or confirmation prompt, so a prompting command hangs the run.

enforcement.run: ! git grep -hIE '^[[:space:]]*(sudo[[:space:]]+)?(ssh|scp)[[:space:]]|apt-get[[:space:]]+install' -- '*.sh' | grep -vE 'BatchMode=yes|apt-get[[:space:]]+install[^#]*[[:space:]]-y' | grep -q .

text: Uncommitted changes pass `git diff --check`: no trailing whitespace, no space-before-tab, no conflict markers.
why: Whitespace noise hides the real change in review and produces diffs that fail on the next editor.

enforcement.run: ! git rev-parse -q --verify HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1 || git diff --check HEAD

text: No tracked file holds a PEM private key block (a line that starts with `-----BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY-----`), outside test fixtures.
why: A private key committed once is readable in every clone and every history that ever held it.

enforcement.run: ! git grep -qIE '^-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----' -- . ':(exclude)test' ':(exclude)tests' ':(exclude)*/fixtures/*'

text: Python never uses a bare `except:`: name the exception the code can handle.
why: A bare except also catches KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit and hides programming errors behind the handler.

enforcement.run: ! git grep -qIE '^[[:space:]]*except[[:space:]]*:' -- '*.py'

text: Python function signatures never default a parameter to a mutable literal (`[]`, `{}`, `set()`): default to `None` and create the value inside.
why: A mutable default is built once and shared by every call, so state leaks between callers.

text: Python outside tests never runs text as code or as a shell line: no `eval(`, `exec(`, `os.system(`, `pickle.load(s)` or `shell=True`.
why: Input that reaches these calls becomes code execution; the argument-list forms of subprocess and the data formats of json need no trust.

enforcement.run: ! git grep -qIE '(^|[^A-Za-z_.])(eval|exec)\(|os\.system\(|pickle\.loads?\(|shell[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*True' -- '*.py' ':(exclude)test' ':(exclude)tests' ':(exclude)__tests__' ':(exclude)*.test.*' ':(exclude)*.spec.*' ':(exclude)*/fixtures/*'

text: A versioned package keeps release notes: a CHANGELOG, HISTORY, NEWS, RELEASE or CHANGES file, or a release workflow.
why: Consumers decide whether to upgrade from what changed; a version number alone does not say.

enforcement.run: if [ -s package.json ] && node -e 'let p={};try{p=JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync("package.json","utf8"))}catch{}process.exit(p.private===true||!p.version||/^0\.0\.0/.test(p.version)?1:0)'; then versioned=1; elif [ -f pyproject.toml ] && grep -qE '^version[[:space:]]*=' pyproject.toml; then versioned=1; else versioned=0; fi; [ "$versioned" = 0 ] || git ls-files | grep -qiE '(^|/)(changelog|changes|history|news|releases?)([^/]*)$|^\.github/(release\.ya?ml|workflows/[^/]*release[^/]*)$'
